query: What is Foundation models for language?
normalized_query: what is foundation models for language
answer: A foundation model for language is a large neural network (typically a Transformer) trained with self-supervision on broad, unlabeled text corpora, so it learns general-purpose linguistic and world knowledge rather than a single task. Because that pretrained base is adaptable, it can be transferred to many downstream tasks—classification, translation, summarization, question answering—via fine-tuning, instruction tuning, or prompting, instead of training a separate model per task. Examples include BERT and GPT-style models; the trade-off is that their scale and shared base mean capabilities, biases, and errors are inherited by every application built on top of them.
